title: Where could the brain keep a symbol?
title_zh: 大脑可能在哪里存放符号？
abstract: Neuroscience routinely describes memories as stored neural symbols, yet durable memory and successful retrieval do not establish a separately accessible symbolic vehicle. I distinguish retention, the claim that a physical change persists and later influences behavior, from symbolic storage, the stronger computational claim that a description can be accessed independently of the operation it specifies. The criterion is functional and system-relative and does not rule out neural activity as access. It requires specifying, before testing, the candidate vehicle, its proposed use, the system boundary, and an endogenous route reaching the vehicle without using it. DNA meets the criterion: replication preserves nucleotide sequence without producing the encoded gene product. Evidence from synapses and circuits establishes persistent, functionally useful organization but has not shown this separation for any neural memory vehicle; in these states, identified reads are executions that modify what they read. Hippocampal replay, neuromodulation, and artificial-network checkpoints show that the verdict depends on the vehicle and operations compared. I agree with Gallistel that intracellular nucleic acid mechanisms could provide a genuine store, but disagree that behavioral precision alone requires one. Maintained coupling, in which memory is sustained by continual recalibration rather than read from a store, offers an alternative whose predictions depend on error source: drift can be corrected where a reference signal remains, but a unique, never-revisited episode offers none. Current evidence favors retention without symbolic storage in synapses and circuits; I propose operational tests that could overturn this verdict. Either way, retention and use remain memory.
abstract_zh: 神经科学常将记忆描述为储存的神经符号，然而持久的记忆和成功的提取并不能确立一个独立可访问的符号载体。我将保持——即物理变化持续存在并后来影响行为的主张——与符号存储相区分，后者是更强的计算主张，即描述可以独立于其所指定的操作而被访问。该标准是功能性的且相对于系统的，并不排除神经活动作为访问途径。它要求在测试前指定候选载体、其拟议用途、系统边界，以及一条不使用该载体即可到达它的内源路径。DNA符合该标准：复制保留核苷酸序列而不产生编码的基因产物。来自突触和电路的证据确立了持久且功能有用的组织，但对于任何神经记忆载体均未显示这种分离；在这些状态下，被识别的读取操作会修改其所读取的内容。海马重放、神经调节和人工网络检查点表明，结论取决于所比较的载体和操作。我同意加利斯泰尔的观点，即细胞内核酸机制可能提供真正的存储，但不同意仅凭行为精确性就需要一个存储。持续耦合——即记忆通过持续重新校准而非从存储中读取来维持——提供了一种替代方案，其预测取决于误差来源：如果存在参考信号，漂移可以被纠正，但一个独特且从不重访的情节则没有提供任何参考信号。目前证据支持突触和电路中的保持而非符号存储；我提出了可能推翻这一结论的操作性测试。无论如何，保持和使用仍然是记忆。
